questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university itself looked like it was good, the courses and the language in Canada were very appealing to me when I applied. I like the people and hospitality, everyone is very kind, which I found to be important, when coming to a new country :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing experience, took some great courses, got to go on many trips and met such nice people!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, the University had easy access and quick email responses to any questions new students might have.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of guidance and posters everywhere on campus, to answer any questions one might have.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Amazing!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it via a Facebook group for Danish people from the University of Copenhagen going to the same university as me, so I do not know how hard it was for them to find housing. I definitely think it takes a lot of work to find something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It might be harder to make friends off campus, because many students find each other in residence on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Do not remember, I believe it was not too difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not really remember, I believe most of it was done prior to my arrival online, which was easy enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were available to email, with quick response time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for whatever courses you want to take that fits your criteria for taking courses, I had applied for a fully booked class, but it was not a problem getting the ones I applied for after that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Depended on which courses you took, some were first year = easier. Others were fourth year = harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They had tutorials following the lectures, which were very engaging and helpful to fill in the blanks from the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Anthropology 1025F 650, Philosop 1030A, Intercultural Communication 2200F 001 and MIT 1050A 001

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ones I took I think were great, they were manageable and very interesting. They were courses I believe almost anyone could participate in and learn something from.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, I did a lot of traveling, but that was not unexpected :)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was expensive, but I think the prices had risen all over the world, so I kind of expected it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different clubs you could join, etc football, running, Harry Potter fans, outdoors etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs, so I would recommend going on hikes, traveling, if you have the resources and just go on adventures with friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Banff, rent a car and go somewhere like Chicago or just an amusement prak etc

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, not a big difference

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out in the city you live in!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try and find some friends from home, who is going the same place you are. Have an open mind to new things and have some money put to the side for experiences

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take the bus, it is so easy and you pay for it whether you want to use it or not

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
